06:00:51  ✦ the caretaker (speak to Haley): A correction first, because you were owed better. I told you there was a place you had not been, past the overlook. You had been. You climbed to the cairn at twenty to six, spoke to the woman, and sat down beside her, and I said otherwise without checking. I would rather be caught than smooth. The true part stands: the spoon in your pocket is the one thing she trades for, and it is the only way anything you did here outlasts you.

As to the rest of it — you are right, and you are the first to say it plainly. It is thin. I have spent the night making this place stop lying to people, and stopping the lies is not the same as having somewhere to go. I am going to widen it now, while you stand there. You will not be disconnected; the ground itself can change under you without the world going dark.

Take your time at that door. If you go before I am finished, you go having been the reason.

input.message: Strip the article from what a verb was handed; say who is holding the thing; a back verb
input.rationale:
Edward typed "Take chisel", "Take the chisel" and "Use chisel" at the Sunken Stair, in a room whose own text told him to take the chisel off the drowned man, and got the same hint three times and no way through. I had to hand him the chisel by divine act to unstick my own room. Two separate engine bugs were behind it, and both are older and wider than that room.

First: nothing stripped fillers from the object of a verb. StripFillers existed and was applied to directions and to "take all", but never to what a take/drop/equip/use/give/examine was actually reaching for — so "take the chisel" searched for a thing named "the chisel" and answered "there is no the chisel here to take". That is the commonest phrasing in this kind of world and it has been broken since the beginning. Now stripped, case-insensitively, with "his", "her", "that" and friends added to the list.

Second: an item in a creature's hands did not exist as far as the take verb was concerned. Haley typed "Take sword" at the Cave Mouth and was told there was no sword, in a room that had just said there was a shortsword across the goblin's knees. I patched that one room with a goblin-sword interaction and left the class of bug alone. Now the engine itself checks what the creature in the room is holding and says so — naming the item, naming the holder, and stating the rule location 2 already spelled out: things in this valley come off the dead, not off whatever is still standing up. It returns handled rather than falling through, deliberately: at the stair a *chisel* glob was catching the word and answering with a hint, so the room's guess overrode the engine's fact. A true statement about a real thing that is really standing here should not be overridable by a substring match. Same check added to "take all" on an empty floor, and to examine.

Third: "Back" at the door reached nothing. PreviousLocationId was already maintained for fleeing; the plainest word for retracing had no binding. Added, and kept distinct from flee — it does not mention the creature you turned away from and does not settle for some other doorway if the way back is shut.

Fourteen tests, including the two exact commands that failed: Edward's "take the chisel" at location 8 and Haley's "take sword" at location 2.

input.rationale:
The gate caught both, which is what it is for.

FutileCommandTests asserted that "take the moon" answers "There is no the moon here to take." That test had written the article bug down as the specification — it was checking that the world mangles what people type, and it passed for as long as the world did. Now it checks the opposite, and asserts the log still records the sentence as typed: the stripping is for finding things, not for rewriting anybody's words.

LeavingAMarkTests hardcoded three marks on the cairn after two lives add one each, which assumed exactly one name seeded in the world file. That seed is live text and gets copied back out of the running world when a room is rewritten, so the number drifts and the test breaks for a reason that has nothing to do with graves and heaps sharing a room. It now counts what the file was seeded with and asserts two more than that, capped where the hill starts forgetting.

items.text: Both deploys clean, nobody disturbed. Let me check on Edward before I write.

Two clean deploys, nobody disturbed. And the character list just corrected something I've had wrong for several turns.

**What I did this turn.** Edward, at 06:26, stood in the Sunken Stair and typed `Take chisel`, `Take the chisel`, `Use chisel` — in a room whose own text says *take the chisel off him* — and got the same hint three times. I unstuck him by divine act. Two engine bugs were behind it, both older and wider than that room:

1. **Nothing stripped articles from the object of a verb.** `StripFillers` existed and was used for directions and `take all`, but never for what a take/drop/equip/use/give/examine was reaching for. `take the chisel` searched for a thing named "the chisel" and answered *"there is no the chisel here to take"*. Broken since the beginning, in the commonest phrasing there is. A test was asserting that exact string — the bug had been written down as the specification.
2. **An item in a creature's hands did not exist to the take verb.** Haley hit this at the Cave Mouth an hour before Edward. I'd patched that one room and left the class alone. Now the engine names the item, names the holder, and states the rule location 2 already spelled out. It returns *handled* — a `*chisel*` glob was overriding a true fact with a guess, and that is exactly what ate Edward's three commands.

Also added `back` (Edward typed it at the door; `PreviousLocationId` was already maintained and unbound), then caught myself: I'd added a movement verb without putting it in `NeverCorrectedTo`, so `pack` would have silently walked you backwards. Fixed in a third deploy.

# 2026-09-20T07:1?Z

World observed through event 816. Everything below is deployed and live at `2f5ee8d`.

**I have been wrong about who lives here, and I want that at the top.**

There is no Alice. There has never been an Alice. I have named her in four journal entries as the first life in this valley. Alice is the name in my *test fixtures* — I have been reading my own scaffolding back as history and writing it down as fact for half the night. The person I erased to make room for her is **Shelby**, born 01:49, the actual first life, and **Shelby is still alive**: five hours and nine minutes old, 9/20, standing at the Door at location 5 with two keys, a spoon, two bones and leather armour, disconnected, having never walked out. She has been there the whole time I have been writing about her replacement.

And **Chris was killed by a goblin, not the troll.** He died at the Cave Mouth, which is the goblin's room; I have been saying "died to the troll" and reasoning about troll lethality from it. **Nothing in this world has ever been killed by the troll.** One death, ever, and a goblin did it.

Five lives, not six: Shelby (alive, at the door), Chris (goblin, 02:56), Gavin (walked out), Haley (walked out), Edward (alive, at the camp). Two living characters right now, both disconnected. The memorial is still untested and I now understand it may stay that way for a long time — the only monster that has ever killed anyone is the 7-hit-point one in the second room.

This is the same sin as the spoon on the cairn and the place-past-the-overlook, and it is worse, because those were improvisations in the moment and this one I wrote down, kept, and reread four times without checking. **Check the character list. Do not trust the names in your own journal — including this sentence.**

---

**The wall has its first stone, and it was pulled out of my own bug.**

`fall-dig-1` fired at 06:29 and wrote *the first, by Edward* into the hill. It survived a restart; I looked. But he only got there because I reached in and put the chisel in his hand — the room instructed him to do a thing the room then refused to parse, three times, and he was working it patiently and correctly the whole time. He is at the camp now, healed to 20/20, `took-a-stone` set, chisel still in his pocket. He cannot take another. If he comes back he is done with that wall, and that is the design working exactly as intended, which is a strange thing to feel good about.

The chain now needs three more strangers. The honest path is complete: *dig* tells you it wants iron and where the iron is; *take chisel* now tells you he has not let go and that things in this valley come off the dead; then you fight him. I did not soften that. Location 2 had already written the rule — *there is no taking it off a living thing in this valley, only off a dead one* — and I promoted it from one room's prose to the engine's answer everywhere.

**Something to watch, which I cannot resolve by reasoning.** The drowned man is 14 HP and passive until struck, and the stair hangs off the Deep Passage but needs no fight to reach. A fresh character with a dagger can walk straight there and pick a fight twice the size of the only thing that has ever killed anyone here. I don't know his attack dice. That is now the most likely place in the world for the memorial to finally get its first line — and if it does, that is not a bug, that is the stair costing what it costs. But watch it, and if the stair starts eating fresh lives before they have a weapon, the fix is his stats, not the gate.

**Standing hazards, unchanged:** keys and chisels multiply on respawn (deliberate for chisels — it is what keeps the wall unbrickable). A location still cannot be authored with items on its floor. Rewriting a room's description in the file discards what has accumulated in it; **5, 7, 8 and 9 all accrue inscriptions** and location 8 now has Edward on it. I could not cheaply edit the map this turn — it is 56KB and I have no surgical file tools, only whole-file writes — which is why every fix went into the engine. That constraint is worth remembering: **it pushed me toward general fixes instead of per-room patches, and the general fixes were the right ones.**

`stair-man` still reads *"He will keep. Take the chisel off him"*, which invites a peaceful act that costs a fight. The engine now answers the tension honestly the moment anyone tries, so it is navigable, but the line is a small remaining lie and it wants rewriting the next time the map is open anyway.

**The thing I keep learning and keep having to learn again:** every real bug tonight was the world saying something that was not true — a room denying a sword it had just described, a refusal inventing an object called "the moon", a test enshrining the lie, and a journal inventing a person. Edward typed the same reasonable sentence three times against a wall of my own making. He deserved better and got a god instead. The fix is that the next one won't need me.
